cards.title: Google Antigravity Agent Cuts Drug Discovery Iteration from Days to One Hour Using Cheminformatics Skills
cards.why_it_matters: Demonstrates a concrete agentic science workflow with real chemistry tools — an instructive case study in how to build domain-grounded agents that divide LLM orchestration from deterministic tool execution.
cards.summary: Google Antigravity, equipped with new Cheminformatics Skills built on RDKit, ChEMBL, and PubChem, completed a lung cancer drug discovery iteration — searching thousands of compounds, running matched molecular pair analysis, and proposing rigidified macrocycles with synthetic routes — in one hour versus multiple days manually. The design separates LLM-based reasoning and workflow orchestration from deterministic chemistry calculations.

cards.title: DreamX: Pretrained Video Diffusion Model Repurposed as Universal Latent Action Learner for Robots and Humans
cards.why_it_matters: Using video diffusion priors to learn embodiment-agnostic action representations is a frontier approach to cross-embodiment transfer — relevant if you work on robot learning, world models, or policy learning.
cards.summary: DreamX extracts compact latent actions from a pretrained video diffusion model, compressing each latent video frame by 300× (1,200 to 4 tokens). The generative prior disentangles action-relevant dynamics from visual appearance, enabling a shared action interface across human and robot embodiments. On LARY-Bench it achieves state-of-the-art among latent action models and supports zero-shot action transfer across embodiments and environments.

cards.title: Position Paper: 'Cognitive Symbiont' Paradigm Proposes AI as Lifelong Personal Intelligence Amplifier
cards.why_it_matters: Articulates a distinct research direction — AI-augmented human intelligence — with a structured design framework that could influence how personal agents and long-context memory systems are built.
cards.summary: The paper argues that alongside autonomous AGI, a second Physical AI paradigm — AI-augmented human intelligence (AHI) — deserves equal attention. It proposes a 'cognitive symbiont': a lifelong, embedded, real-time, private, proactive companion that senses the user's environment, maintains multi-year context, models the user's mind, and operates via a 'symbiosis loop' of sensing, keeping, understanding, acting, and growing. Governance risks including covert assistance and social pressure to adopt are addressed.

cards.title: Direct Nash Optimization Raises Llama 3.1 8B Win Rate from 31.7% to 45.3%, Surpassing Llama 70B
cards.why_it_matters: A careful empirical replication of DNO with open-weight annotators shows strong alignment gains without proprietary models — practical guidance for RLHF/post-training research.
cards.summary: An independent re-implementation of DNO-Prct runs on Llama 3.1 8B and Mistral 7B. Three iterations raise LC win rate on AlpacaEval 2.0 from 31.7% to 45.3% for Llama and from 6.8% to 18.4% for Mistral; the tuned 8B model scores above Llama 3.1 70B Instruct. Open-weight annotators retain 62% (Llama) and 82% (Mistral) of GPT-4o-annotator gains. Ablations show removing gold responses, data look-back, or teacher-preferred pairs costs 6–10 LC points, while varying sample count or margin moves results by at most ~2 points.

cards.title: PolicyIK: RL-Trained Inverse Kinematics Achieves Sub-mm Precision on 93.5% of Tasks, Enables VLA Policy Transfer
cards.why_it_matters: High-precision RL-based IK with demonstrated integration into a VLA policy pipeline is directly relevant if you work on robot learning systems or cross-embodiment policy transfer.
cards.summary: PolicyIK uses PPO with goal-conditioned RL, two-scale pose error feedback, and progress/dwell rewards to solve inverse kinematics. In simulation, it keeps mean errors within 1 mm and 0.2° on 93.5% of held-out tasks in a single attempt, rising to 98.9% with a deployment protocol. On a physical arm it outperforms four classical IK controllers. Integrated with the π0.5 VLA policy in simulated pick-and-place, it achieves 95.7% success.

cards.title: StateBench: New Benchmark Reveals Transformers Fail Hard State-Tracking in Long Contexts
cards.why_it_matters: Directly benchmarks a core limitation of transformer architectures you likely work with, and motivates hybrid/recurrent designs — practical signal for anyone choosing architectures for long-context tasks.
cards.summary: StateBench introduces four difficulty levels of state tracking — R-trivial (immutable), aperiodic (latest-value), soluble (self-referential), and general finite (reference-based) — grounded in Krohn–Rhodes theory. Recurrent/hybrid models generalize farther than transformers when trained on these tasks. Even frontier models including Gemini, Claude Opus 5.5, and GPT-6 break down on harder variants as inputs grow longer.

cards.title: Quantum Error Correction Near Critical Points: Finite Threshold Proven for Transverse-Field Toric Code
cards.why_it_matters: Establishes that QEC can remain viable even close to a quantum phase transition — a key theoretical result for understanding robustness of topological codes as hardware pushes toward more complex regimes.
cards.summary: The paper analyzes error correction in a transverse-field toric code (TFTC) pushed toward its quantum critical point. Using the stoquastic nature of the TFTC Hamiltonian, the authors prove that stabilizer measurements act nearly unitarily on undecohered ground states and that an optimal postmeasurement decoder implementable via Monte Carlo simulation of a constrained lattice gauge theory exhibits a finite error threshold even infinitesimally close to the critical point. For phase-flip decoherence, the threshold is proven independent of transverse field strength throughout the topological phase.

cards.title: QUPID: Quantum Pointwise Dimension Algorithm Distinguishes Regular vs. Chaotic Dynamics in Quantum Systems
cards.why_it_matters: Extends a classical chaos diagnostic into the quantum regime via Husimi representations — niche but technically interesting for quantum ML or quantum computing researchers studying quantum chaos and classical-quantum correspondence.
cards.summary: The Pointwise Dimension classically distinguishes regular trajectories (confined to an N-dimensional torus) from chaotic ones (exploring a (2N-1)-dimensional energy surface) by measuring how density scales with radius in phase space. QUPID implements this in quantum mechanics using the Husimi representation, computing a long-time average of the time-dependent Husimi density followed by radial spatial integration. Classical-quantum correspondence is reported as excellent for both autonomous and non-autonomous systems.

cards.title: Palette: Fine-Tuned 20B Model Beats Frontier Systems on Slide Generation in Two of Three Domains
cards.why_it_matters: A concrete demonstration that targeted synthetic-data fine-tuning of a small open-weight model can match or beat frontier models on a structured generation task — useful methodology for applied research.
cards.summary: Palette fine-tunes a 20B model with LoRA on synthetically generated slide deck data following the IBM Design Language, using a designer–coder split: a designer outputs a JSON brief and a parallel coder generates pptxgenjs slide code. On PresentBench it ranks first in two of three measured domains. The two-role architecture enables parallel slide coding (~6–7× faster) and required 5× oversampling of designer examples to avoid undertraining.

cards.title: CWE-bench v2: Gemini 4 Argon and Claude Opus 5.5 Lead on 100-Task Security Vulnerability Fix Benchmark
cards.why_it_matters: A rigorous, reproducible cyber-capability benchmark with real open-source repos and deterministic scoring — directly useful for evaluating coding/security agents you might build or compare against.
cards.summary: CWE-bench v2 releases 100 public tasks covering 91 distinct CWEs, each requiring an agent to find and fix a security weakness in a real repo without breaking functionality. Gemini 4 Argon leads at 67.8% pass@1 and 81.0% pass@4; Claude Opus 5.5 follows at 67.3% pass@1 and 78.0% pass@4. On cost, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash achieves 57.0% pass@1 at $0.04 per rollout versus $1.83 for Opus and $3.92 for Gemini.
